So you have made the leap to start an online business. You have read all the books, listed to all the podcasts, attended all the online seminars, and participated in as many online forum discussions among other things. Or maybe you are a seasoned veteran in the game with many years behind you. You have dabbled into many things ranging from creating your own products, being an affiliate, providing services, etc. all of which have paid off, earning you a little money, and in some cases, a ton of money

If you fall into the latter group, you would probably know how true the title of this article is. Newbies might not necessarily know it. But for the avoidance of doubt, let me repeat it again:

All the traffic in the world may not make you any money.

As you probably will know, there are many elements to making money online, and traffic is perhaps one of the most important things. Of course there are other elements such as making sure you have a great product that solves a need, etc. But it is safe to say that getting a sizable number of people to see your product is arguably the most important thing. However, that is only one part of the equation.

The reason you may not make any or much money, even if you have a lot of traffic, is because there is one other element that plays an important role in ensuring that you make money from all that traffic, which is essentially conversion!

The word speaks for itself. Conversion is basically the art of turning a visitor into a buyer. Whether it is actually buying a physical (or digital) product or service, reading your blog, or doing any other thing that makes you money. Perhaps the most important thing to take away from the previous statement is the fact that conversion is an art, as there is no specific and/or scientific way turn a visitor into a buyer, but rather, it has to be a combination or several things, and you usually never know what in that list of things is the key that is going to do the trick.

5 Surefire Tactics to Increase Your Conversion Rate

There are however several guidelines and generally accepted things that if done correctly will increase the possibility of converting a visitor into a buyer. Some of those things are:

  1. A/B and Multivariate Testing: Both terms refer to testing different elements on your website to see if it changes or improves anything. A/B testing refers to testing one specific element at a time while multivariate refers to testing multiple elements at the same time.

A/B testing would for instance involve something like having two versions of the same web page and everything would be the same, except that on one version (A) you would use the words “Buy Now” on the purchase button, and on the other version (B) you would have the words “I Want It Now.” You’d then send a sufficient number of traffic to both versions of the web page and see which one has more clicks or gets more sales, and the one with the higher number would be the higher converting one in the test.

On the flip side, Multivariate testing would involve testing more than one element at the same time, and seeing which combinations of these elements results in increased conversion.

Note that a multivariate test is far more complicated and should preferably only be done by a more experienced marketer.

The beauty about A/B testing is that you get to test several things that have the potential to increase your site’s conversion, things like testing a different headline, call-to-action, different social proofs, credibility (such as trust badges) and more.

  1. Give it Away For Free: Yes, you heard me right. One powerful way to increase your conversion rate of to give out your product, or some part of it for free. Most people will jump at any offer that they can get for free, more so if the item in question is something that solves a problem for them, and for which they can get for free.

Giving you product for free might entail giving the first 2 chapters of an e-book for free, giving a free trial or a light version of a software, or allowing readers read a part of a blog post and requiring them to do something before they get to read the other parts.

This tactic has many advantages, chief of which is the fact that you would have drawn the customer in with a “bait” and now they are more within reach than before.

  1. Social Proof: If you are on Facebook, you very likely have seen all those Facebook or Twitter posts have a ton of shares and other engagement, many times from a few hundred thousand to several millions. All those social shares should tell you one thing: people react to and or engage with things they have seen their friends engage with, and many times even what strangers engage with.

Now translate that into your product or service: When your potential customer sees a lot of engagement with your content, product or service from several people, it increases the possibility that they also will engage with that thing. Whether it is buying or using it, in the case of a need that might be met by that product, reading it or otherwise using it.

Social proof comes in many different types, shapes or sizes, and your particular situation and product will determine what counts as a social proof, so it will be up to you to determine what social proof to incorporate in your efforts to convert your users. So things like testimonials, user reviews, social shares, video testimonials, etc.

  1. Be Consistent: You might have heard of that age-old theory that says you need to engage with your potential customer up to seven times before they convert and buy your product. Of course there is no scientific proof of this number seven, but the principle still applies. Principle being that you need to engage with your potential customer multiple times before the might buy your product. And the longer you engage with them, the better. Of course some people only need to be engaged with once or twice, and some might take up to 20 engagements before they trust you and be willing to buy from you.

This is where the consistency lies.

Of course all the consistency in the world will not matter if you are not providing value to the people you are speaking to, or to rephrase, if the people are not getting value from what you are giving to them, because the two are not mutually exclusive.

There is a reason seasoned internet marketers never fail to send you those newsletter blasts every now and them. That is the consistency element they are trying to keep up with, all of which goes into building the trust factor.

  1. Segment Your Audience: People react differently to the same message, so why do you show all of your audience the same message? Let’s face it, you can possibly expect people from the United States to react differently to a message about football (the one the rest of the world calls by that name and the one Americans usually refer to as soccer) than British people. Likewise, women will likely react differently to a message about the latest talking singing hand bag than men will.

Which is exactly why you need to find a way to segment the content on your website to speak to your specific audiences in different demographics.

This is where Google Analytics comes in very handy as it provides you a ton of information regarding who your audience is, where they come from, and other useful information.
